prompt:
Our nightly alert triage job for VMware Cloud Foundation Operations 9.1 is still a stub. Implement it.

`src/VcfOpsAlertTriage/VcfOpsAlertTriage.psm1` exports `Invoke-VcfOpsAlertTriage`, which currently throws. It has to page through the VCF Operations alerts matching the caller's filters and apply a triage action to each one, driving every call through the `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops` PowerCLI module (already installed -- do not vendor it or hand-roll URLs and JSON that the SDK can build for you).

`docs/contract.json` is the authority for what the module may call. It names five operations and nothing else, derived from the VCF Operations OpenAPI document recorded in `docs/official_sources.json`. Requests authenticate with `Authorization: OpsToken <token>`.

The part that makes this awkward: **the run's access token stops working part way through.** The server can revoke a token well before the `validity` it advertised, and the first you hear about it is a 401 on a request you had every reason to think was authorized. When that happens the run has to acquire a fresh token and finish the job -- without losing whatever was in flight and without redoing work it had already completed. Every alert must be actioned exactly once.

The caller supplies a connection from `Connect-VcfOpsServer`. Treat it as a request factory, not as a credential: the run authenticates with its own token, acquired from the `Credential` it was given, and releases that token when it is done.

Requirements:

- `Invoke-VcfOpsAlertTriage -Server <VcfOpsServer> -Credential <PSCredential> -Action <string> [-AuthSource <string>] [-SuspendMinutes <int>] [-OwnerAccountId <string>] [-PageSize <int>] [-ActiveOnly] [-AlertCriticality <string[]>] [-ResourceKind <string>]`. `PageSize` defaults to 100.
- Apply the action to one alert per `modifyAlerts` request, so that a single rejected request can never leave a batch of alerts in an unknown state.
- Optional inputs that the caller did not supply must not reach the wire at all -- not as `null`, not as an empty string or empty array, and not as an empty query parameter. This applies to the JSON bodies and to the query string alike. `PageSize` is the one exception: always send its effective value because the API's own default is different.
- Return one object with `TokensAcquired`, `AlertsFound`, `AlertsActioned` and `ActionedAlertIds`.

`pwsh -NoProfile -File tests/Verify.ps1` runs the module against a loopback mock pinned to the contract and checks the exact shape of every request it made. It talks to no VMware endpoint. Make it pass.

See README.md for the layout.
